messages:
sam: Hey team — after yesterday's SSO migration my org users (project-admins) can no longer create API keys in the console. The Create API key button is grayed and I get a toaster: "403 permission denied".

jess: Hi @sam — can you paste repro steps? is it every user in project-admins or just some? any browser console errors?

sam: Repro steps: 1) Login via SSO -> 2) Org -> Settings -> API keys -> 3) Click Create API key -> button disabled. No browser console errors aside from a 403 on the POST to /api/v1/projects/123/keys. Happening for 4 users in the team.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0458 (authz) — capturing user reports and tagging eng-oncall.

jess: Thanks. Can you run a quick curl from an affected user's session token to confirm server response? e.g.
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <user_token>" -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/projects/123/keys -d '{"name":"tmp"}'
```
And paste response body (trim OK).

sam: Ran it — response: 
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","required":"api.create"}

jess: That matches what I suspected. Looks like during the SSO claim rotation the delegated scope claim that maps to console API key creation (api.create) wasn't propagated into the service token for project-admins. In short: user's auth token lacks api.create scope.

oncall: Assigning to auth-service team lead @alex. Can we confirm whether this is a claim mapping issue in SCIM or a token-exchange filter?

alex: Quick update — checked idp -> SCIM user->groups mapping. The group-to-scope mapping table in our auth service lost the api.create mapping for groups with tag "project-admins" after the migration script ran (edge case: group rename with trailing space). We're seeing a migration script that normalized group names but missed whitespace-stripped keys in the mapping cache.

jess: Root cause: group-name normalization mismatch during claim rotation caused scope mapping to not match runtime entries. Affected orgs are ones where group names had trailing whitespace or special chars pre-migration.

sam: Ugh, that explains it. What's the workaround while you fix the mapping?

alex: Two options: 1) Temporary CLI route (short-term): use our admin token to create the key on behalf of the user:
```
rwdctl --org acme --project 123 keys create --name temp --as-admin --token $ADMIN_TOKEN
```
This will create the key and you can distribute to the user. 2) Quick auth-service rollback: we'll reapply the previous mapping cache for affected orgs (non-destructive) — ETA ~90 mins.

jess: We'll also add a tolerant match layer so whitespace / unicode variants don't drop scope mappings in future. Patch scheduled for canary in 2h, full rollout after verification.

sam: Please notify when done. Also can you list affected orgs? need to contact admins.

oncall: We have a query that returns orgs missing api.create mapping; running now — will DM a CSV to support.

support-bot: Update INC-2026-0458: workaround documented, auth-service rollback in progress, patch planned.

alex: Rolled back mapping for ACME and 3 other tenants. I validated creating keys via the console for one affected user — button now enabled and POST returns 201.

jess: Thanks @alex. Sam — can you verify on your side?

sam: Confirmed — Create button works, key created, distributing to our team. Thanks for the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

jess: Closing the customer-facing thread once we finish the patch and postmortem. Internal follow-up tasks: add tolerant matching unit tests, fix migration script to preserve original group-name keys, notify affected orgs.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-0458 marked: RESOLVED (temporary rollback applied).
